property_summary: Any caller other than the original owner cannot change the owner in the correct contract, but can in the buggy one.
After any call to setOwner by the current owner, the owner state variable should equal the argument passed to setOwner; the mutant breaks this by setting owner to zero regardless of input.

After a call to setOwner by the current owner, the state variable 'owner' must equal the passed argument (_owner) in the correct contract; the buggy version fails this because it drops the assignment, leaving owner unchanged.
The owner address can only be changed by the current owner; the bug allows any non-owner caller to change the owner.

After any successful setOwner call, the owner must equal the argument; the mutant makes every setOwner call revert so owner never changes, violating the rule when msg.sender is the current owner and the new address differs from the current owner.

For any caller, a successful setOwner call (one that does not revert) must update owner to the passed argument; the buggy modifier always reverts, so no call can ever succeed and change owner, violating the rule when the caller is the current owner and the new address differs.

For any caller, a call to setOwner that does not revert must result in owner equalling the argument; the mutant always reverts, so no call can succeed, violating the rule when the caller is the current owner.
If setOwner is called by the current owner, it must succeed (not revert); the mutant always reverts, so a call by the current owner fails.
For any caller that is the owner, setOwner(args) returns true in the reference contract, whereas the buggy version returns false.
For any owner who calls setOwner with any address, the return value must be true; the mutant returns false instead.
For any owner who calls setOwner with any address, the return value must be true; the mutant returns false instead.
For any call to setOwner that does not revert, the reference contract always returns true, while the mutant returns false.
For any owner, setOwner(address) must change owner to the provided address parameter; the bug ignores the parameter and sets owner to msg.sender.
Only the contract owner can change the owner state variable; the buggy version allows any non-owner caller to change it.
